Laura —

Finance view: Net60 is higher credit risk than our default marketplace expectation (Net30). We can accept Net60 for private offers but only with:
- Signed credit agreement or purchase order with payment milestones,
- 25% upfront payment on contract signature,
- Credit hold clause if invoices >45 days overdue.

On rev-share: moving to 20% (10ppt reduction) materially impacts our channel economics. The attached pricing model shows a ~+35% gross cost per ARR for year one under a 20% rev-share + 45% discount. If we must concede, we need either a higher minimum commit ($350k) or a clawback if ARR < $275k at 12 months.

I recommend proposing a compromise: 25% rev-share + 40% discount + 25% upfront. That preserves margin while giving the customer upside.

-Vanessa
Head of Finance, Commercial Partnerships
